LIDAR antenna constraint — marjum-2026-07¶

A viewing interface for the platform-LIDAR constraint on the antenna position. It caches nothing: the returns come from the campaign pointing table, the antenna prior from the campaign's published geometry release, the DEM and the fitted result from the terrain/ checkout, and the ray march is marjum_lidar_constraint.march itself rather than a copy. Pointing it at a different release or a different fit is an edit to section 1 only.

Sections 3 and 4 are static, slide-ready figures at the published fit. Section 5 is the interactive explorer: every free parameter in the fit is exposed, including the ones the memo held fixed.

What this is for¶

Two claims in the memo are worth pushing on by hand rather than taking on faith:

  1. The east/north position. The memo held dE/dN at the photogrammetric value; letting them move absorbs some of the second-dip mismatch but does not reproduce across data subsets. The sliders show the trade directly — in particular how daz and dN swap against each other.
  2. The DEM-error hypothesis. The memo argues the residual second-dip depth is terrain-model error, because a rigid translation can displace a dip but not deepen one. The DEM bias slider lets you try to fix it that way and see what it costs elsewhere.

Replaces the cached version¶

Until 2026-09-21 this notebook read a 0.3 MB lidar_explorer_cache.npz holding a DEM subtile and a copy of the returns, and re-implemented the ray march in numpy. The cache never shipped beside the notebook, so the notebook did not run here at all; the reimplementation was a second definition of the model that could drift from the memo. Both are gone. The DEM loads in ~0.5 s and a full march takes milliseconds, so the cache bought nothing.

1. Inputs¶

Everything below is read at run time. Nothing is a literal that a new geometry release or a re-run fit would leave stale.

def save(fig, name):
    """Write `fig` to FIGDIR/name.{png,pdf} when SAVE_FIGURES is set."""

        return

    print('wrote', FIGDIR / f'{name}.png')

# --- LIDAR returns, straight from the campaign pointing table ----------------
RET = M.load_returns()
EL, AZ, D, T = RET['el'], RET['az'], RET['d'], RET['t']
DWELL, SWEEP = RET['plateau'], RET['sweep']
NEARF, PLUMB = RET['nearfield'], RET['plumb']
TMIN = T.min()

# --- antenna prior, from the campaign's published geometry release -----------
# Not a literal: the release is the authority, and reading it here means a new
# release changes this notebook's prior without an edit.

RELEASE = RELEASES[-1]
SHARED = json.loads((RELEASE / 'shared.json').read_text())

DEM = MarjumDEM(cache_file=str(TERRAIN / 'marjum_dem_sw.npz'))

2. The model¶

Two independent pieces of geometry, both exposed below.

The terrain ray march. The LIDAR sits at 90° to the antenna boresight, so only the LIDAR arm matters here — a LIDAR ground return is not evidence that the antenna pointed at the ground. The ray's zenith angle is el − el_nadir + 180 and its azimuth is az + daz. March it from the antenna position in 0.5 m increments and take the first cell at or below the ray.

The plumb line. The near-field returns are the LIDAR striking the PVC frame carrying the antenna box. The frame hangs under gravity, so a ray at angle chi to it strikes it at x / sin(chi). That is what measures el_nadir — and the link checkbox ties the two panels together, so moving the plumb line moves the terrain model too. That coupling is the memo's §4 result; watch what a degree does.

Note x/sin(chi) and h/cos(chi−90) are the same function, so this fit cannot distinguish a vertical line from a plane perpendicular to it. It measures the direction, not the shape.

In [3]:
def march(origin, el, az_pot, el_nadir, bias=0.0):
    """Ranges from `marjum_lidar_constraint.march`, with an optional DEM bias.

    `bias` raises or lowers the whole terrain; it is the blunt instrument the
    memo's DEM-error hypothesis is tested with. It is applied by lowering the
    ray origin instead of copying the 320 MB DEM, which is equivalent for a
    first-intersection search and costs nothing.
    """
    o = np.asarray(origin, float) - np.array([0.0, 0.0, bias])
    return M.march(DEM, o, el, az_pot, el_nadir)


def ground_points(origin, el, az_pot, el_nadir, bias=0.0):
    """Where each ray meets the DEM (ENU, m). Undoes the `bias` origin shift
    so the returned points are in true coordinates rather than shifted ones."""
    o = np.asarray(origin, float) - np.array([0.0, 0.0, bias])
    points, _ = M.ground_points(DEM, o, el, az_pot, el_nadir)
    return points + np.array([0.0, 0.0, bias])


def plumb_model(el, x, el_vertical):
    """Range to a vertical member at perpendicular offset `x`."""
    return x / np.abs(np.sin(np.radians(el - el_vertical)))


def hillshade(z, res, az_deg=315.0, alt_deg=45.0):
    gy, gx = np.gradient(z, res, res)
    slope = np.pi / 2.0 - np.arctan(np.hypot(gx, gy))
    aspect = np.arctan2(-gx, gy)
    az, al = np.radians(360.0 - az_deg + 90.0), np.radians(alt_deg)
    v = (np.sin(al) * np.sin(slope)
         + np.cos(al) * np.cos(slope) * np.cos(az - aspect))
    return np.clip(v, 0, 1)


# Hillshade only the neighbourhood the rays can reach, at half resolution: the
# full 10000x8000 DEM takes ~10 s to shade and nothing outside RMAX is visible.
PAD_M = M.RMAX + 40.0
_c0 = int(round((ANT[0] - PAD_M) / DEM.res)) + DEM.e0_px
_c1 = int(round((ANT[0] + PAD_M) / DEM.res)) + DEM.e0_px
_r0 = int(round((ANT[1] - PAD_M) / DEM.res)) + DEM.n0_px
_r1 = int(round((ANT[1] + PAD_M) / DEM.res)) + DEM.n0_px
_sub = DEM.data[_r0:_r1:2, _c0:_c1:2].astype(np.float64)
# The DEM is int32, so elevation is quantised to 1 m and a raw gradient turns
# every quantisation step into speckle. A 3-pixel box smooth before shading
# removes it. This affects the backdrop only -- the ray march uses DEM.data.
_k = np.ones((3, 3)) / 9.0
_pad = np.pad(_sub, 1, mode='edge')
_smooth = sum(_k[i, j] * _pad[i:i + _sub.shape[0], j:j + _sub.shape[1]]
              for i in range(3) for j in range(3))
HS = hillshade(_smooth, DEM.res * 2)
HS_EXTENT = ((_c0 - DEM.e0_px) * DEM.res, (_c1 - DEM.e0_px) * DEM.res,
             (_r0 - DEM.n0_px) * DEM.res, (_r1 - DEM.n0_px) * DEM.res)
print('hillshade %s over E %.0f..%.0f  N %.0f..%.0f'
      % (HS.shape, *HS_EXTENT))


def masks(nf_cut, lo, hi):
    near = D < nf_cut
    dwell = DWELL & ~near
    sweep = SWEEP & ~near
    return near, dwell, sweep, sweep & (D > lo) & (D < hi)


def evaluate(p):
    """Predicted ranges, residuals and the memo's scalar diagnostics."""
    near, dwell, sweep, score = masks(p['nf'], p['lo'], p['hi'])
    origin = ANT + np.array([p['dE'], p['dN'], p['dU']])
    sel = sweep | dwell
    pred = np.full(len(EL), np.nan)
    pred[sel] = march(origin, EL[sel], AZ[sel] + p['daz'], p['eln'], bias=p['bias'])
    resid = D - pred
    out = dict(pred=pred, resid=resid, near=near, dwell=dwell, sweep=sweep,
               score=score, origin=origin)
    out['nhit'] = int(np.isfinite(pred[sweep]).sum())
    out['mad'] = float(np.nanmedian(np.abs(resid[score]))) if score.sum() else np.nan
    for name, (a, b) in WIN.items():
        m = score & (EL >= a) & (EL < b)
        out[name] = float(np.nanmedian(resid[m])) if m.sum() else np.nan
    out['dwell_med'] = float(np.nanmedian(resid[dwell])) if dwell.sum() else np.nan
    return out


print('model helpers ready')

In [4]:
POP_COLOR = {'sweep': 'tab:blue', 'dwell': 'tab:orange', 'near': 'tab:red'}
POP_LABEL = {'sweep': 'sweep (canyon walls)', 'dwell': 'dwell (near-nadir)',
             'near': 'near-field (support frame)'}


def _ordered(mask, xaxis):
    """x, and a NaN-break mask for the gaps that would otherwise be drawn."""
    x = EL[mask] if xaxis == 'el' else (T[mask] - TMIN) / 60.0
    order = np.argsort(x)
    xs = x[order]
    # Break the connecting line across large x gaps; otherwise the two
    # near-field clusters (el ~ -103 and ~ +74) are joined by a line straight
    # across the plot, which reads as data.
    gap = np.r_[False, np.diff(xs) > (5.0 if xaxis == 'el' else 1.0)]
    return order, xs, gap


def draw_profile(R, p, ax_range, ax_resid, populations=('sweep',), xaxis='el',
                 windows=SHOW_WINDOWS, yscale=RANGE_YSCALE):
    """The range profile and its residual, shared by the figures and the explorer."""
    if windows and xaxis == 'el':
        for name, shade in (('W1', '0.93'), ('W2', '0.84'), ('W3', '0.93')):
            for axis in (ax_range, ax_resid):
                axis.axvspan(*WIN[name], color=shade, zorder=0)
            ax_range.annotate('%s\n%g\u2013%g\u00b0' % (name, *WIN[name]),
                              xy=(np.mean(WIN[name]), 1.005),
                              xycoords=('data', 'axes fraction'), ha='center',
                              va='bottom', fontsize=11, color='0.35',
                              linespacing=1.15)
    for name in populations:
        mask = {'sweep': R['sweep'], 'dwell': R['dwell'], 'near': R['near']}[name]
        if not mask.sum():
            continue
        order, xs, gap = _ordered(mask, xaxis)

        def brk(values):
            out = np.asarray(values, float).copy()
            out[gap] = np.nan
            return out

        ax_range.plot(xs, brk(D[mask][order]), 'o-', ms=5, lw=1.0,
                      color=POP_COLOR[name], label=POP_LABEL[name] + ', measured')
        if name != 'near':
            ax_range.plot(xs, brk(R['pred'][mask][order]), 'x--', ms=5, lw=1.0,
                          color='0.25', label=POP_LABEL[name] + ', DEM model')
            ax_resid.plot(xs, brk(R['resid'][mask][order]), 'o-', ms=4, lw=1.0,
                          color=POP_COLOR[name])
    ax_resid.axhline(0, color='0.55', lw=1.0)
    ax_range.set_yscale(yscale)
    ax_range.set_ylabel('Range [m]')
    if yscale == 'linear':
        # Clip to the terrain returns. A few sweep samples reach 200 m with no
        # model; on a linear axis they flatten the dips this figure is about.
        modelled = np.isfinite(R['pred'])
        if modelled.any():
            hi = np.nanmax(np.r_[D[modelled], R['pred'][modelled]])
            lo = np.nanmin(np.r_[D[modelled], R['pred'][modelled]])
            ax_range.set_ylim(max(0.0, lo - 0.08 * (hi - lo)), hi + 0.08 * (hi - lo))
    ax_range.legend(loc='upper left', ncol=2, fontsize=12)
    ax_resid.set_ylabel('Measured − model [m]')
    ax_resid.set_ylim(-20, 20)
    ax_resid.set_xlabel('Platform elevation [deg]' if xaxis == 'el'
                        else 'Minutes from first return')
    # Confine x to where the march produced a model. A handful of sweep returns
    # sit near el -100 with no terrain intersection; left in, they stretch the
    # axis until the 30-150 deg profile this figure is about is unreadable.
    modelled = np.isfinite(R['pred'])
    if modelled.any():
        x = EL[modelled] if xaxis == 'el' else (T[modelled] - TMIN) / 60.0
        pad = 0.04 * (x.max() - x.min())
        # Both axes: the static figure builds them with add_subplot, not sharex.
        for axis in (ax_range, ax_resid):
            axis.set_xlim(x.min() - pad, x.max() + pad)


def draw_plumb(p, ax):
    """The near-field, up-looking cluster against the hanging-frame model."""
    mask = NEARF & (EL < -90)
    el, rng = EL[mask], D[mask]
    grid = np.linspace(el.min() - 1.5, el.max() + 1.5, 300)
    ax.plot(el, rng, 'o', ms=7, color='tab:red', label='near-field, up-looking')
    ax.plot(grid, plumb_model(grid, p['px'], p['pel']), '-', color='0.2', lw=2.0,
            label='plumb: x=%.3f m, vertical at el=%.2f°' % (p['px'], p['pel']))
    rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean((plumb_model(el, p['px'], p['pel']) - rng) ** 2)))
    ax.set_ylim(0, max(3.0, rng.max() * 1.6))
    ax.set_xlabel('Platform elevation [deg]')
    ax.set_ylabel('Range [m]')
    ax.legend(loc='upper right', fontsize=12)
    return rms


def draw_map(R, p, ax, fig):
    """Ray footprint on the hillshade, coloured by |residual|."""
    ax.imshow(HS, cmap='gray', origin='lower', extent=HS_EXTENT, zorder=0)
    mask = R['sweep']
    pts = ground_points(R['origin'], EL[mask], AZ[mask] + p['daz'], p['eln'],
                        bias=p['bias'])
    good = np.isfinite(pts[:, 0])
    points = ax.scatter(pts[good, 0], pts[good, 1],
                        c=np.clip(np.abs(R['resid'][mask][good]), 0, 20),
                        s=34, cmap='autumn_r', edgecolors='k', linewidths=0.3,
                        zorder=3)
    fig.colorbar(points, ax=ax, label='|residual| [m]', shrink=0.85, pad=0.02)
    ax.plot(*ANT[:2], 'c+', ms=14, mew=3, zorder=4, label='photogrammetric prior')
    ax.plot(*R['origin'][:2], 'b*', ms=18, mec='k', zorder=5, label='tuned position')
    ax.set_xlim(min(np.nanmin(pts[good, 0]), ANT[0]) - 40,
                max(np.nanmax(pts[good, 0]), ANT[0]) + 40)
    ax.set_ylim(min(np.nanmin(pts[good, 1]), ANT[1]) - 40,
                max(np.nanmax(pts[good, 1]), ANT[1]) + 40)
    ax.set_aspect('equal')
    ax.set_xlabel('East [m]')
    ax.set_ylabel('North [m]')
    ax.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=12, frameon=True, framealpha=0.85,
              facecolor='white', edgecolor='none')


def scorecard(R):
    """The memo's diagnostics, with the published value beside each."""
    ref = ENCFG['published']
    lines = ['rays hitting terrain %d / %d      scored %d'
             % (R['nhit'], int(R['sweep'].sum()), int(R['score'].sum())),
             'shape MAD   %7.3f m   (published %+.3f)' % (R['mad'], ref['MAD'])]
    for name in ('W1', 'W2', 'W3'):
        note = '   <-- the second dip' if name == 'W2' else ''
        lines.append('%s median   %+7.3f m   (published %+.3f)  el %g-%g%s'
                     % (name, R[name], ref[name], *WIN[name], note))
    lines.append('dwell median residual %+.3f m' % R['dwell_med'])
    return '\n'.join(lines)


PUBLISHED = dict(daz=PUB['daz_deg'], eln=PUB['el_nadir_deg'], dU=PUB['dU_m'],
                 dE=0.0, dN=0.0, bias=0.0, nf=M.NEARFIELD_MAX, lo=80.0, hi=130.0,
                 px=PLUMBFIT['offset_x_m'], pel=PLUMBFIT['el_vertical_deg'])

3. Range profile at the published fit¶

W1, W2, W3 are not named features. They are three contiguous elevation bins covering the upper half of the sweep — W1 88–105°, W2 105–122°, W3 122–140° — and the fit is scored by the median residual in each one separately rather than by one number over the whole sweep. The reason is that the two failure modes they separate look identical in a single MAD:

  • a position error displaces the whole profile, so W1, W2 and W3 all move the same way together;
  • a terrain-model error distorts it, so they move independently.

W2 is the bin holding the second dip, and it is the one that does not come out: it sits at −6.4 m while W1 and W3 are within ±1.1 m. That asymmetry is the memo's evidence for DEM error over a mis-placed antenna — and it is what the explorer in section 5 is for.

             'daz %.2f°, el_nadir %.2f°, dU %+.2f m — shape MAD %.2f m'

    1, 2, figsize=(17, 8), constrained_layout=True,
    gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1.35, 1]))
draw_map(R_pub, PUBLISHED, ax_map, fig)
ax_map.set_title('Ray footprint on the DEM, coloured by |residual|')
rms = draw_plumb(PUBLISHED, ax_plumb)
ax_plumb.set_title('Plumb line from near-field returns — rms %.3f m' % rms)
save(fig, 'lidar_footprint_and_plumb')
plt.show()

5. Interactive explorer¶

Tips for exploring by hand

  • el_nadir is the dominant knob. It moves the fit about 1 m of apparent antenna height per degree, and it is what changed the memo's answer between revisions 1 and 2. The plumb line measures it as 92.25° ± 1.4°; revision 1 assumed 87.68°. Try both.
  • Watch daz and dN trade. Push dN to −6 and re-snap daz: it drops from ~43° to ~36°. That coupling is why the azimuth registration cannot be quoted tighter than ~36–47° once E/N is free.
  • Score on the shape set (measured range 80–130 m). That window is chosen from the measured values alone, so it cannot favour a model. The W2 readout is the second dip — the feature under discussion.
  • DEM bias shifts the whole terrain up or down. Deliberately a blunt instrument: if the second-dip mismatch were a simple terrain offset this would fix it. Watch what it does to W1 and W3 while you try.
  • snap daz/dU grid-searches azimuth and height at your current E/N and el_nadir. Use it after moving E/N so you compare best-achievable against best-achievable rather than against a stale azimuth.
  • Near-field samples are excluded from scoring by the near-field cut; they are the support frame, not terrain. Drop the cut to 0 to see what including them does.

The sliders need a live kernel with ipywidgets. In a rendered HTML or PDF copy this section shows its last executed state; sections 3 and 4 are the figures meant to be read statically.

def params():

    return dict(daz=daz_w.value, eln=eln, dU=dU_w.value, dE=dE_w.value,
                dN=dN_w.value, bias=bias_w.value, nf=nf_w.value,

def redraw(*_):
    if _busy['on']:
        return
    p = params()
    R = evaluate(p)
    with out:
        out.clear_output(wait=True)
        nrow = 2 + int(plumb_w.value)
        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(13, 5.4 + 3.2 * (nrow - 2)))
        gs = fig.add_gridspec(nrow, 1, height_ratios=[2, 1] + [1.6] * (nrow - 2),
                              hspace=0.55)
        ax_range, ax_resid = fig.add_subplot(gs[0]), fig.add_subplot(gs[1])
        draw_profile(R, p, ax_range, ax_resid, populations=pop_w.value,
                     xaxis=xaxis_w.value, windows=True)
        ax_range.set_title('daz %.2f | el_nadir %.2f | dE %+.2f dN %+.2f dU %+.2f '
                           '| DEM bias %+.2f'
                           % (p['daz'], p['eln'], p['dE'], p['dN'], p['dU'], p['bias']),
                           fontsize=14)
        if plumb_w.value:
            rms = draw_plumb(p, fig.add_subplot(gs[2]))
            print('plumb rms %.3f m   (published %.3f)' % (rms, PLUMBFIT['rms_resid_m']))
        plt.show()

        if map_w.value:
            # Its own figure: an equal-aspect map squashed into a wide gridspec
            # row comes out postage-stamp sized.
            figm, axm = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.0, 7.2))
            draw_map(R, p, axm, figm)
            plt.show()
        print(scorecard(R))


def on_snap(_):
    # Marches only the scored rays: the objective never looks at the dwell, and
    # including it made this button take ~16 s.
    _busy['on'] = True
    snap_b.description = 'snapping...'
    try:
        p = params()
        _, _, _, score = masks(p['nf'], p['lo'], p['hi'])
        el_s, az_s, d_s = EL[score], AZ[score], D[score]
        best, best_value = None, np.inf
        for a in np.arange(max(0.0, p['daz'] - 12), p['daz'] + 12.01, 1.0):
            for u in np.arange(p['dU'] - 3, p['dU'] + 3.01, 0.25):
                origin = ANT + np.array([p['dE'], p['dN'], u])
                pred = march(origin, el_s, az_s + a, p['eln'], bias=p['bias'])
                ok = np.isfinite(pred)
                if ok.sum() < 0.6 * len(el_s):
                    continue
                value = float(np.median(np.abs(d_s[ok] - pred[ok])))
                if value < best_value:
                    best, best_value = (a, u), value
        if best:
            daz_w.value, dU_w.value = float(best[0]), float(best[1])
    finally:
        _busy['on'] = False
        snap_b.description = 'snap daz/dU'
    redraw()


def _set(daz, eln, dU, dE, dN):
    _busy['on'] = True
    daz_w.value, eln_w.value, dU_w.value = daz, eln, dU
    dE_w.value, dN_w.value, bias_w.value = dE, dN, 0.0
    _busy['on'] = False
    redraw()


snap_b.on_click(on_snap)

Three things worth trying¶

  1. Reset: revision 1, then reset: published. That is the +4.6° change in el_nadir from the plumb line. Watch the dwell median residual change sign (−1.47 → +1.32 m) and the second dip shift.
  2. Reset: published, then drag dN to −6 and press snap daz/dU. W2 improves from −6.4 to about −3.9 and daz falls to ~36°. Then look at the deep part of the second dip near el 118: it is still ~6 m short. That is the point the memo makes — a translation displaces a dip, it does not deepen one.
  3. Try to close that gap with DEM bias. You can null W2, but watch W1 and W3 go the other way as you do it. If you find a setting that flattens all three at once, the memo's DEM-error conclusion is wrong and I want to know.

Provenance and caveats¶

  • Returns: marjum-2026-07/pointing/pointing_table_v0.npz, selected by marjum_lidar_constraint.load_returns with GOOD_MASK = 0x17B — everything except HEIGHT_ASSUMED and AZ_SLIP_EVENT, which are provenance rather than defect. 250.00 m exactly is the out-of-range sentinel, not a measurement.
  • Antenna prior: the latest marjum-2026-07/imgs/fits/vNNNN_marjum_geometry/shared.json. It is a provisional deterministic fit and carries no uncertainty interval; the legacy MCMC pilot is unconverged.
  • DEM: terrain/marjum_dem_sw.npz, int32 on a 0.5 m grid, sampled nearest-neighbour. Ground elevation is therefore quantised to 1 m, which is comparable to the disagreements being measured. The cache carries its own e0_px/n0_px working-grid anchor; marjum_bundle.working_grid predates that and would shift it a second time, so it is deliberately not used here.
  • Published fit: terrain/lidar_constraint_v2/summary.json. Section 1 re-derives its MAD and W1/W2/W3 medians from the live inputs and prints both, so a drift in any input shows up as a mismatch rather than silently.
  • Populations must not be pooled. The dwell is one very well-repeated range measurement, not a profile: it pins height at ~1:1 and says almost nothing about azimuth. The sweep carries the horizontal information.
  • Is this the current geometry? Yes, in the sense that both inputs are the newest published values, but note their dates. The antenna point estimate (1655.868, 2030.923, 1777.397) is the 2026-09-13 photogrammetric fit, carried identically by geometry release v0001 and by terrain/antenna_position_bracket.json (antenna_position@v1, bound 1.7 m, not a posterior sigma). The LIDAR registration — daz 43.0°, el_nadir 92.25° from the plumb line, dU +0.75 m — is the 2026-09-15 lidar_constraint_v2 fit. Nothing in either location has changed since 2026-09-15, so if later work revised the consensus, it has not been written anywhere this notebook can read.
  • curation/antenna_position.json does not exist. Its schema has been in the campaign since 2026-09-13, but the position-of-record product it defines was never written, so there is no era-scoped antenna position with a posterior to read. This notebook falls back to the geometry release's shared.json. When that product lands, section 1 should read it instead.
  • This notebook writes no products.
